description.purpose: The container this person's channels are instantiated into. It ships empty and open: no cells, no ports, no contract of its own. A CHANNEL is how the person is reached -- a chat account, a screen, a phone line -- and since GH #454 it belongs to the PERSON rather than to one of their agents. That is the whole reason this container is here and not one level down: a bot owned by a generation is one agent's bot, a second agent of the same person cannot be reached through it, and a screen two agents both draw on has no owner at all.
description.use_when: Never on its own -- it travels with the member level. One channel is normally ONE node instantiated into this container at the name it is known by: `telegram` and `slack` are one connector cell each (telegram-connector@2.0.1, a proxy), `display-<screen>` is the screen channel and `voice` the phone one. The name is the value of `context.channel` the turn carries, and it is what the answer is routed back by, so it is a fact of the wiring rather than a label. TRANSIT, two lanes in each direction and no more -- IN, from the channel up into the level: `turn` (a raw inbound message, re-stamped to `in_turn` by the level's own edge into ./firewall) and `error` (the channel's own failure, which the level re-emits). OUT, from the level down into the channel: `answer` (what an assistant said, addressed by `context.channel`) and nothing else. The level ships both halves of the first pair and the level-side half of the second; what an instantiating mutation adds is the node and the two edges that bind it to this container by name.
description.not_in_scope: No ports, because a sealed hive refuses exactly the endpoints a channel instantiation needs (hive_port_boundary) -- and the pairing edge between this container and a connector below it is such an endpoint. No slot: GH #285's slot governs an address that does not exist, and this container does exist, so the declared unbound word could never fire -- see unbound_slot_behaviour in crates/meclaw-colony/src/colony.rs, which steps aside as soon as the target is a registered hive scope. No params.contract either, for the same load-bearing reason ./assistants declares none: this container is wired by its own level the moment the member is instantiated, so mutation::hive_contract::check_lane_doors sees a WIRED hive from birth (hive_path_is_wired) and would then owe a door inside for every declared accepts lane -- and a member with no channel yet is a legitimate state. No cells: what stands in this container is a channel, and a channel is instantiated, never shipped. And no ADDRESS RULE of its own: which assistant a turn was meant for is decided by the channel's outbound edge, which stamps `context.assistant`, and by the per-assistant edges inside ./assistants that read it. This container carries the turn and reads nothing in it.
